name: FRED
description: US and international economic time series from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis: rates, prices, employment, output and money, with the full revision history behind each figure.

tools.name: Category
tools.description: Call to confirm what a category id is before walking down from it, or with no argument to land on the root. The only category endpoint that takes no real-time period, so what it returns is always the current name.

tools.name: Child categories
tools.description: The rung of the walk from the root to a series list. It descends one level per call, so getting from the root to a leaf takes several. Nothing here pages: a category with many children returns all of them.

options.about: End of the real-time period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. Set 9999-12-31 for the full revision history.
options.name: realtime_end

tools.name: Release table
tools.description: Call when the layout matters - which line of a published table a series sits on, and what nests under what. This is the only capability here that answers with a tree rather than a list, so a caller that walks `key` plus `paginated` has to special-case it: descend `elements`, then each element's `children`.

options.about: The release to read, for example 53 for Gross Domestic Product. Find one with `releases/releases`.
options.name: release_id

options.about: The element to read. Omit for the root element of the release's table tree.
options.name: element_id

options.about: Attach observation values to elements whose `type` is series. Only those elements gain them.
options.name: include_observation_values

options.about: The observation date to read values at, YYYY-MM-DD. Only meaningful with `include_observation_values`.
options.name: observation_date

response.about: Structurally unlike every other capability here: not an envelope around a list. The body is the requested element itself, and its `elements` field is an object keyed by stringified element id rather than an array, with each element carrying a recursive `children`. There is no real-time period and no paging. Two things to expect: `release_id` is a string at the top level and a number inside each element, and asking for the root - no `element_id` - returns only `release_id` and `elements`, without `name` or `element_id`.

fields.about: Name of the requested element. Present only when `element_id` was given: asking for the root returns `release_id` and `elements` alone.

The one required argument is the one that is optional on `tags/tags`, and `tag_group_id` does not accept `cc` here. Tag names may contain spaces, so a value like `monetary aggregates;weekly` needs the space URL-encoded and only the `;` treated as a separator.
